# Franclloyd D. Dagdag — Full-Stack Web Developer

> Portfolio of Franclloyd D. Dagdag, a full-stack web developer from the Philippines
> specializing in scalable system architecture, complex problem solving, and precision
> engineering. Builds end-to-end products across React, Next.js, Node.js, Python, and
> Laravel, with a focus on performance, maintainability, and clean system design.

Franclloyd has shipped government-scale platforms (Internal Audit Management System,
Procurement Management System, blockchain-backed financial audit) and rebuilt client
web presences for speed and SEO. B.S. Information Technology, Caraga State University
(magna cum laude, 2023).

## Pages

- [Home / Portfolio](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/): Overview, skills, experience, featured projects, and contact.
- [Blog — Case Studies](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog): Index of in-depth case studies on real client work.
- [Two Custom Sites in Three Days](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/two-sites-three-days): Two complete, custom React websites built for one client (Kiona) in 72 hours — a premium Kangen water wellness brand (HydraWellnessLux) and a high-ticket sales coaching platform (LimitlessKBL). Two distinct brand identities on a fixed three-day deadline, both shipped on time; a look at the reusable component system and workflow that makes fast, fully custom delivery possible without cutting corners.
- [Guardion — Elite Protection Brand Built in One Week](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/guardion): Launching Guardion, an elite Australian close-protection and investigations firm, from a thin single-page starter site to a full bilingual brand platform on Next.js + Supabase with a custom CMS. Built in one week with an English/Chinese (中文) experience and SEO-first architecture; PageSpeed rose from a 75 baseline to a perfect 100 on desktop, with performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO all scoring 100. A referral client, with a data-driven results follow-up planned for the next quarter.
- [Acro Refrigeration Case Study](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/acro-refrigeration): Migrating a 50+ year Australian refrigeration company from a slow WordPress site to a Next.js + Supabase platform with a custom CMS — 100+ blog posts migrated, ~10x faster load times, and zero SEO regression.
- [Acro Refrigeration — 90 Days Later](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/acro-refrigeration-90-days): A data-driven follow-up 90 days after the Acro Refrigeration rebuild — visitors up 110% month over month, 91.5K Google search impressions, a PageSpeed score holding at 95 performance / 100 SEO, and early AI-assistant discovery (chatgpt.com referrals, a 3/3 Agentic Browsing score).
- [HVACR Group — One Client, Four Websites](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/hvacr-group): After the Acro Refrigeration rebuild, the same Australian group (HVACR Group) returned to redesign three more of their brands — Shelair, HVACR Group, and Koolacube — off WordPress onto one shared Next.js + Supabase stack. Every site scores 90+ performance and 100 SEO; Koolacube's performance rose from 44 to 93.
- [WordPress vs. Hardcoded](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/wordpress-vs-hardcoded): A field-notes breakdown contrasting WordPress with hand-built, hardcoded websites — where custom code gains its edge in speed, security, SEO, and ownership, and how WordPress becomes a disadvantage over the long run.
- [Are AI Website Builders Good for SEO?](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/ai-website-builders-seo): An honest breakdown of AI website builders (Lovable, Bolt, v0) and SEO — why client-rendered single-page apps, thin metadata, and missing structured data quietly hurt rankings, whether AI-generated content is good for SEO, and how search is evolving (not dying) in 2026 with AI Overviews, GEO, and answer-engine optimization. Answers the "People also ask" questions on AI builders and SEO.
- [Framer AI vs. Custom-Coded](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/framer-ai-vs-custom-coded): An honest breakdown of Framer AI versus a custom-coded website — what Framer AI is, whether it is good for SEO (better than app-style builders, but with a real ceiling), whether Framer uses coding, how it compares to Figma and WordPress, and how to tell a custom-built site from a template. Explains that any platform gives you eligibility, not rankings — content, keyword strategy, authority, and information architecture are the human half of SEO no tool automates. Covers where Framer genuinely wins, where platform lock-in and SEO/functionality ceilings cost you, and when to graduate from Framer to custom code. Answers the "People also ask" questions on Framer AI, SEO platforms, and hosting.
- [How to Set Up SEO for a Website](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/how-to-set-up-seo-for-a-website): A developer's step-by-step guide to the on-site SEO setup for a website — the technical and on-page layers, in order: mapping one keyword to each page, making the site crawlable and server-rendered (not a JavaScript shell), unique title tags and meta descriptions, one H1 with logical headings, clean URLs, internal links and image alt text, technical must-haves (HTTPS, canonical tags, structured data/schema, mobile-first, hreflang), passing Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), submitting to Google Search Console and requesting indexing, then verifying and troubleshooting why a page isn't indexed. A focused companion to the broader channel-by-channel "How to Set Up SEO" guide. Answers the "People also ask" questions on setting up SEO for a website, on-page vs. technical SEO, website speed, and why a site isn't showing up on Google.
- [How to Set Up SEO](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/how-to-set-up-seo): A practical, step-by-step guide to setting up SEO across every channel. Explains the three layers of SEO (technical, on-page, off-page), then walks through the setup in order: the website foundation (crawlable HTML, title tags and meta descriptions, headings, XML sitemap, robots.txt, canonical tags, structured data, HTTPS, Core Web Vitals, Google Search Console), Google Business Profile for local SEO, optimizing social media profiles, LinkedIn personal and company pages, then YouTube, directories/citations, AI answer engines (GEO/AEO), and owned channels — plus how to measure with Search Console and Analytics. Answers the "People also ask" questions on how to set up SEO for beginners.
- [Website vs. Social Media](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/website-vs-social-media): The honest breakdown of website vs. social media for business — a website is property you own (domain, design, data, Google-indexed, permanent) while social media is rented space a platform controls. Covers whether social media alone is enough, the 5 advantages of a website, whether you need a website to sell, the real disadvantages and common website red flags, and why small businesses still need a website in 2026. Answers the "People also ask" questions on website vs. social media.
- [wp2shell — Pre-Auth RCE in WordPress Core](https://www.daggerbuilds.com/blog/wp2shell-wordpress-core-rce): Analysis of wp2shell (CVE-2026-60137 + CVE-2026-63030), a pre-authentication remote code execution chain in WordPress core disclosed July 17, 2026, affecting versions 6.9.x and 7.0.x with no plugins required. Covers how to check exposure, patch to 6.9.5 / 7.0.2, check a site for compromise, and why core-level flaws make every install vulnerable at the same instant.
